title: Student Learning-Support Preferences in the Age of Generative AI
content: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used by students for academic support, but it remains unclear how students value AI-based support compared with other forms of teaching and peer support. This study examined learning-support preferences among 366 second-year computing students at Kaunas University of Technology who were surveyed in 2025 and 2026 using a repeated cross-sectional design. Ten learning-support preferences and GenAI use frequency were analyzed using non-parametric tests, equivalence tests, rank correlations, and ordinal logistic regression. Students rated practical examples, clearly structured information, and peer assistance highest, whereas preference for using AI tools in learning was moderate and social media was rated lowest. Between the 2025 and 2026 Software Systems cohorts, weekly or daily GenAI use increased from 58.1% to 77.1%, yet all ten preferences were statistically equivalent across cohorts and across computing programs. More frequent GenAI use was associated with stronger preference for AI-supported learning (ρ = .284; OR = 1.93, 95% CI [1.58, 2.35]), whereas its associations with peer support, group work, and most other forms of support were negligible. The findings suggest that GenAI currently functions as an additional source of learning support rather than a replacement for teaching and peer support.
